Guards the fresh requirement, the context-slot bound on covered intervals, and the metadata-driven verify span.

expected_survivors_note: None. The mint header-floor mutant, declared in the first pass as redundantly covered by condition-1, is now killed: the two guards refuse with DIFFERENT messages, and a test asserting which refusal occurs tells them apart -- the codex seat's point in review, the same one-message-two-conditions lesson as b9c. Covered-elsewhere was the honest first label; a distinguishing test was the better answer.
pytest_args: not ReserveScopeTests and not DecoderOrchestrationTests and not PublicationGateTests
pytest_args_reason: Those three classes open research/b9a_outcomes.sqlite read-only -- the burned cohort, an UNTRACKED evidence artifact absent from the sweep's tracked-only staged tree, so they cannot run there and the unmutated baseline fails on them. They exercise decode orchestration, reserve scoping and publication gates, none of which this cutoff change touches. COST, per the framework's rule: any mutant killable ONLY through one of these excluded tests reports as a survivor here and must earn its own in-memory test rather than a declaration. Every declared mutant is in the cutoff/boundary path, covered by in-memory boundary tests and the new FreshCutoff/CoveredInterval/VerifySpan classes, so none should so survive; if one does, it is a real coverage gap, not an artifact of the exclusion.
